title: The PageRank Citation Ranking: Bringing Order to the Web
why: Connects graph centrality, Markov chains, and ranking before learned representations.
exercise: Implement power iteration with teleportation; test dangling nodes and sensitivity to the damping factor.

title: Laplacian Eigenmaps and Spectral Techniques for Embedding and Clustering
why: Introduces the graph Laplacian as a bridge between geometry, embeddings, and spectral learning.
exercise: Compute two-dimensional spectral embeddings of a small graph; compare neighborhoods with a random layout.

title: DeepWalk: Online Learning of Social Representations
why: Turns short random walks into a practical unsupervised representation-learning pipeline.
exercise: Implement walk generation and skip-gram training; evaluate node classification with a fixed split.

title: LINE: Large-scale Information Network Embedding
why: Separates first-order and second-order proximity and introduces efficient edge sampling.
exercise: Implement the two proximity objectives and compare their concatenation on link prediction.

title: node2vec: Scalable Feature Learning for Networks
why: Shows how biased walks trade off local neighborhoods and structural roles.
exercise: Sweep return and exploration parameters against DeepWalk using identical downstream evaluation.

title: Network Embedding as Matrix Factorization: Unifying DeepWalk, LINE, PTE, and node2vec
why: Explains random-walk embeddings through matrix factorization and spectral graph structure.
exercise: Construct NetMF on a small graph and compare it with sampled DeepWalk embeddings.

title: Spectral Networks and Locally Connected Networks on Graphs
why: Provides a historical starting point for learned convolution in a graph Fourier basis.
exercise: Implement one spectral filtering layer and measure how its parameters depend on the graph basis.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks on Graphs with Fast Localized Spectral Filtering
why: Replaces expensive eigendecomposition with localized polynomial filters.
exercise: Implement Chebyshev recurrence; compare polynomial order, receptive field, runtime, and accuracy.

title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
authors: Thomas N. Kipf and Max Welling
why: Establishes a compact, reproducible baseline for learning from node features and edges.
exercise: Implement a two-layer GCN; ablate self-loops, normalization, and feature-only baselines.

title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
why: Introduces neighborhood sampling and aggregation for generalization to unseen nodes.
exercise: Implement mean aggregation with sampling and evaluate a genuine inductive node split.

title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry
why: Unifies many graph architectures through message, update, and readout functions.
exercise: Build a small edge-aware message-passing model for one molecular regression target.

title: Graph Attention Networks
why: Introduces learned neighborhood weighting and multi-head attention.
exercise: Implement masked graph attention; compare heads and attention dropout with GCN.

title: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?
why: Relates aggregation to graph isomorphism and motivates the Graph Isomorphism Network.
exercise: Implement GIN and test sum versus mean aggregation on controlled multiset and graph examples.

title: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning with Differentiable Pooling
why: Introduces learned graph coarsening for prediction over entire graphs.
exercise: Implement one DiffPool stage and compare it with global mean pooling under matched budgets.

title: Gated Graph Sequence Neural Networks
why: Connects recurrent gated updates to reasoning on graph structure.
exercise: Implement gated propagation on a synthetic reachability or shortest-path task.

title: Simplifying Graph Convolutional Networks
why: Tests whether nonlinear depth is necessary and supplies a strong inexpensive baseline.
exercise: Reproduce SGC and compare propagation depth, training time, and accuracy against GCN.

title: Predict then Propagate: Graph Neural Networks meet Personalized PageRank
why: Connects the opening PageRank material to decoupled neural prediction and diffusion.
exercise: Implement APPNP and sweep teleportation probability and propagation steps.

title: Geom-GCN: Geometric Graph Convolutional Networks
why: Explores geometric neighborhoods when ordinary local aggregation misses useful structure.
exercise: Compare geometric and adjacency neighborhoods using documented public data splits.

title: Beyond Homophily in Graph Neural Networks: Current Limitations and Effective Designs
why: Studies graphs whose connected nodes differ and motivates separating ego and neighbor information.
exercise: Implement an H2GCN-style baseline and vary homophily on synthetic graphs.

title: Pitfalls of Graph Neural Network Evaluation
why: Makes split choice, fair tuning, and uncertainty central to claims about model quality.
exercise: Implement a shared evaluation harness for GCN and GAT across several splits and random seeds.

title: Weisfeiler and Leman Go Neural: Higher-order Graph Neural Networks
why: Examines the expressivity ceiling of standard message passing and higher-order alternatives.
exercise: Construct graph pairs that defeat 1-WL and compare a small higher-order model.

title: On the Bottleneck of Graph Neural Networks and its Practical Implications
why: Introduces over-squashing as a failure of information transmission across graph bottlenecks.
exercise: Reproduce a small long-range task and compare added shortcuts with increased hidden dimension.

title: Understanding over-squashing and bottlenecks on graphs via curvature
why: Gives a geometric account of bottlenecks and a principled graph-rewiring approach.
exercise: Implement or adapt curvature-based rewiring; compare against random edge additions at equal budget.

title: PairNorm: Tackling Oversmoothing in GNNs
why: Separates representation collapse with depth from other GNN limitations.
exercise: Implement PairNorm and plot node-embedding distances and accuracy as depth increases.

title: Cluster-GCN: An Efficient Algorithm for Training Deep and Large Graph Convolutional Networks
why: Uses graph partitions to make minibatch training memory-efficient.
exercise: Train on cluster batches; report peak memory, epoch time, and accuracy against neighbor sampling.

title: GraphSAINT: Graph Sampling Based Inductive Learning Method
why: Studies subgraph sampling with normalization to improve training efficiency.
exercise: Implement one subgraph sampler and test the contribution of sampling normalization.

title: SIGN: Scalable Inception Graph Neural Networks
venue: ICML Graph Representation Learning and Beyond Workshop
why: Shows how precomputed graph filters can trade storage for fast training.
exercise: Precompute multiple propagation scales and include preprocessing time in comparisons with GraphSAGE.

title: Open Graph Benchmark: Datasets for Machine Learning on Graphs
why: Supplies task-specific datasets, realistic splits, and standardized evaluators.
exercise: Implement an OGB baseline and document why its official split and metric match the task.

title: Deep Graph Infomax
why: Introduces node representation learning through local-global contrast.
exercise: Implement DGI and test feature corruption with a frozen linear evaluation protocol.

title: Graph Contrastive Learning with Augmentations
why: Makes graph augmentations a central design choice in contrastive pretraining.
exercise: Implement two graph augmentations and assess whether they preserve labels on the chosen dataset.

title: Large-Scale Representation Learning on Graphs via Bootstrapping
why: Explores self-supervision without explicit negative pairs and its memory implications.
exercise: Implement a teacher-student moving-average update and ablate stop-gradient or predictor design.

title: GraphMAE: Self-Supervised Masked Graph Autoencoders
why: Uses masked feature reconstruction as an alternative to contrastive objectives.
exercise: Implement masked reconstruction and compare masking ratios with a supervised baseline.

title: Modeling Relational Data with Graph Convolutional Networks
why: Extends message passing to typed relations and knowledge-graph completion.
exercise: Implement basis-decomposed R-GCN on a small relational dataset with leakage-aware edge splits.

title: Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network
why: Separates attention over neighbors from attention over semantic meta-paths.
exercise: Implement two meta-path channels and compare learned semantic attention with uniform weighting.

title: Heterogeneous Graph Transformer
why: Combines type-dependent attention, temporal encodings, and heterogeneous sampling.
exercise: Implement type-specific projections and ablate node and relation types on a manageable graph.

title: Inductive Representation Learning on Temporal Graphs
why: Introduces temporal attention with continuous-time encodings.
exercise: Implement TGAT-style temporal neighbors and verify every prediction uses only past events.

title: Temporal Graph Networks for Deep Learning on Dynamic Graphs
venue: ICML Graph Representation Learning and Beyond Workshop
why: Introduces event-driven memory for learning on changing graphs.
exercise: Implement a reduced TGN pipeline and compare memory updates with a memory-free temporal model.

title: A Generalization of Transformer Networks to Graphs
authors: Vijay Prakash Dwivedi and Xavier Bresson
venue: AAAI Workshop on Deep Learning on Graphs
why: Introduces a clear graph-transformer baseline with Laplacian positional information.
exercise: Implement sparse graph attention with Laplacian encodings and test the effect of removing positions.

title: Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation?
why: Shows how structural encodings make global attention useful for graph prediction.
exercise: Implement a compact Graphormer and ablate degree and shortest-path encodings.

title: Rethinking Graph Transformers with Spectral Attention
why: Studies learned spectral position encodings and fully connected attention.
exercise: Implement a small spectral encoder and examine eigenvector-sign perturbations and graph-size cost.

title: Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer
why: Combines local message passing, global attention, and position or structure encodings.
exercise: Implement one GPS block and perform a three-component ablation under a fixed parameter budget.

title: Exphormer: Sparse Transformers for Graphs
why: Uses sparse attention patterns to make graph transformers practical on larger graphs.
exercise: Implement expander-style sparse attention and compare memory and accuracy with dense attention.

title: Generative Adversarial Nets
why: Provides the adversarial-learning prerequisite; this paper itself is not a graph model.
exercise: Implement a small GAN on a toy distribution and diagnose instability before attempting graph generation.

title: GraphGAN: Graph Representation Learning with Generative Adversarial Nets
why: Applies adversarial training to connectivity distributions for graph embeddings.
exercise: Implement a small generator-discriminator link model and compare with a random-walk embedding baseline.

title: MolGAN: An implicit generative model for small molecular graphs
authors: Nicola De Cao and Thomas Kipf
venue: ICML Workshop on Theoretical Foundations and Applications of Deep Generative Models
why: Combines adversarial graph generation with property objectives and exposes mode collapse.
exercise: Implement a reduced small-molecule generator; report validity, uniqueness, novelty, and diversity.

title: GraphRNN: Generating Realistic Graphs with Deep Auto-regressive Models
why: Provides an autoregressive alternative to adversarial graph generation.
exercise: Implement a small sequential graph generator and compare degree and clustering distributions.

title: DiGress: Discrete Denoising Diffusion for Graph Generation
why: Introduces categorical diffusion for graph structure and attributes.
exercise: Implement a reduced discrete diffusion model on small synthetic graphs and evaluate structural validity.

title: GNNExplainer: Generating Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
why: Explores which subgraphs and features support a GNN prediction.
exercise: Implement explanation masks on a motif dataset; measure fidelity, sparsity, and stability.

title: Adversarial Attacks on Graph Neural Networks via Meta Learning
why: Studies sensitivity to training-graph perturbations and motivates robust evaluation.
exercise: On a public benchmark, compare controlled edge perturbations with random edits and report accuracy degradation.

title: Temporal Graph Benchmark for Machine Learning on Temporal Graphs
why: Makes temporal splits, realistic negative candidates, and simple baselines part of credible research.
exercise: Implement an official temporal baseline and compare it with a recent-history heuristic.
